problem_type: The group header carried a redundant logo, a color dot, a collapse button and a more button outside the frame, and several of their functions also lived in the group toolbar and the right-click menu, so the same action had two entries that could drift apart
symptom: User 10-10: the redundant logo at the top-left of the group frame had already moved into the group toolbar; the group chrome showed duplicated entries.
direct_cause: The header was designed outside the frame in a separate branch (outside prop) that kept chrome from an older design after the toolbar and context menu absorbed its functions; no check listed which header function had a destination.
class_root: Feature census for a UI surface lived only in a plan document; nothing tied each removed or moved function to a destination, so a redesign could drop a function or keep a duplicate entry without any test noticing.
migration: Header moved inside the frame; outside branch, color dot, collapse button and more button deleted in the same change. Toolbar gained a trailing more button opening the same FrameContextMenu. Description moved into the menu edit state. Generate-all added inside the frame on the same runFrameAction path.
affected_population: Anyone who used the outside label, the collapse button or the more button
Anyone expecting description editing on double click of the label
entry_points: GroupFrameHeader.tsx: in-frame header and edit draft
invariants: Every header function has a destination in the frame, the toolbar or the context menu (F1–F19)
Generate all uses the same execution path as the toolbar generate
Deleting a group from the menu deletes its members in one undo step

door_reduction.why_not: Each surface keeps its own entry point; what was removed is the duplicate header entry for collapse and more.

residual_risks: The census is a source assertion: it proves each function has code at its destination, not that the user finds it. The real-app walk covers the visible paths for zh-light and en-dark only.
internal_only_reason: Destinations are product decisions made by the user on 10-10 (P1–P3); no external protocol is involved.

recurrence.reason: Each redesign of the group chrome moved functions between the frame, the toolbar and the menu without a list; the outside-label design had accumulated duplicates over several releases.

generality_proof: Each header function must map to a census row; the census test asserts that each row points at live code, so a removed function without a destination fails the test.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Single menu for rename, description, collapse, generate, timeline, dissolve and delete on a group.

prevention.invariant: Each group header function has a live destination (F1–F19).
prevention.failure_mode: A header function is removed or moved without a destination, or a removed entry comes back.

legacy_paths.rationale: Removed declarations are inside GroupFrameHeader.tsx (outside branch, color dot, collapse and more buttons); no file was deleted, and the outside prop is gone with them.
